context: First exposure to French for 6-7 year olds

lessons.title: Bonjour tout le monde
lessons.oneGoal: Students will recognize and respond to basic greetings in French

structure.opening: Wave and say 'Bonjour!' enthusiastically. Watch their faces - do they look curious or overwhelmed?
structure.mainActivity: Greeting circle game - pass a special object around, each person says 'Bonjour' to the next. Use gestures and smiles heavily.
structure.closing: Practice 'Au revoir' with waving motions. End with familiar English to ease transition.

decisionPoints.if: Students seem overwhelmed by French sounds
decisionPoints.then: Use more gestures, slower pace, and mix in familiar English words. Focus on 'Bonjour' only.

decisionPoints.if: Students are eager and responding well
decisionPoints.then: Add 'Comment ça va?' with simple gesture responses (thumbs up/down).

decisionPoints.if: Energy is low or attention scattered
decisionPoints.then: Turn it into a movement game - hop to say 'Bonjour', march to say 'Au revoir'.

whenThingsGoWrong.studentsSilent: Model enthusiastically yourself, don't pressure responses. Use puppet or stuffed animal to 'help' demonstrate.
whenThingsGoWrong.tooMuchChatter: Establish simple hand signal for attention. Use the greeting words to regain focus.
whenThingsGoWrong.someStudentsWithdraw: Let them observe. Give high-fives instead of verbal responses.

materials: Special greeting object (ball, stuffed animal, or colorful item)
Simple visual cards with waving gestures
Optional: puppet or classroom mascot

lessons.title: Comment tu t'appelles?
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand the question 'What's your name?' and hear name responses

structure.opening: Review 'Bonjour' from yesterday. Introduce yourself: 'Je m'appelle Madame...' with clear gestures to yourself.
structure.mainActivity: Name circle - ask each student 'Comment tu t'appelles?' Give them option to say name in French or just say their name. No pressure.
structure.closing: Play quick name memory game - point to students and class says their names.

decisionPoints.then: Have them ask each other. Support with gestures and prompting.
Use name tags, point to names while saying them. More visual support.

decisionPoints.if: Students want to try saying 'Je m'appelle'
decisionPoints.then: Celebrate attempts, don't correct pronunciation. Focus on communication over accuracy.

whenThingsGoWrong.studentsConfused: Switch to just pointing and saying names clearly. Come back to question later.
whenThingsGoWrong.oneStudentDominates: Use turn-taking object. Gentle redirection to 'listen to friends'.
whenThingsGoWrong.forgetsNames: Perfectly normal! Use name tags or have students help each other.

materials: Name tags or cards
Turn-taking object
Poster with your name written clearly

lessons.title: Les couleurs magiques
lessons.oneGoal: Students will recognize and point to basic colors when named in French

structure.opening: Quick greeting review. Show colorful items around room - get their attention on colors.
structure.mainActivity: Color hunt - call out colors in French, students find and point to items. Start with one color, add gradually.
structure.closing: Circle time - each student shares one thing in the room that's their favorite color (you say the French word).

decisionPoints.then: Add simple phrases like 'Je vois du rouge' while pointing.
Use colored paper or objects. Hold up colors and repeat names multiple times.
Play 'Jacques dit' (Simon Says) with colors - 'Jacques dit touchez quelque chose de bleu'.

whenThingsGoWrong.cantFindColors: Have backup colored paper or crayons ready. Point to obvious examples.
whenThingsGoWrong.tooExcitedByHunt: Establish simple rules first. Use calm voice to model behavior.
whenThingsGoWrong.confusingColors: Focus on two colors only. Repeat many times with clear examples.

materials: Colored paper squares (red, blue, yellow, green)
Crayons or markers in target colors
Colorful classroom objects for reference

lessons.title: Compter ensemble
lessons.oneGoal: Students will recognize numbers 1-5 in French through songs and games

structure.opening: Color review - show colors and have students call out in French or point.
structure.mainActivity: Counting with fingers and movements. Simple song or chant with numbers. Count classroom objects together.
structure.closing: Number line walk - students step on numbers while class counts in French.

decisionPoints.then: Add simple math concepts - show 2 crayons plus 1 crayon equals 3 crayons.
Use jumping, clapping, or dancing to reinforce each number.

decisionPoints.if: Five numbers feel like too many
decisionPoints.then: Focus on 1-3 today. Quality over quantity.

whenThingsGoWrong.cantRememberNumbers: Use fingers consistently. Show numbers visually. Practice just 1-2 numbers.
whenThingsGoWrong.mixingFrenchAndEnglish: Completely normal! Gently model French version without correction.
whenThingsGoWrong.lostIntetest: Turn into active game - hop the number of times, clap the number of times.

materials: Number cards 1-5
Small counting objects (blocks, bears, etc.)
Number line on floor (tape or chalk)
Fingers for counting!

lessons.title: Ma famille
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify family members when shown pictures and hear French names

structure.opening: Numbers warm-up - quick count to 5 with actions.
structure.mainActivity: Family pictures - show diverse family photos, name family members in French. Students can share about their families if comfortable.
structure.closing: Simple family song or chant. Draw quick family picture while saying French words.

decisionPoints.if: Students connect easily to family vocabulary
decisionPoints.then: Ask simple questions like 'Où est maman?' while looking at pictures.
Repeat words many times with pictures. Use gestures for each family member.

decisionPoints.if: Students want to share about their families
decisionPoints.then: Support in English, then repeat key words in French. Honor all family structures.

whenThingsGoWrong.sensitiveFamilyTopics: Keep focus on pictures, not personal details. Some students may just listen.
whenThingsGoWrong.studentsOvershare: Gentle redirection to the French words. 'That's wonderful - maman!'
whenThingsGoWrong.vocabularyTooAbstract: Use toy family figures or simple drawings. Make it concrete.

materials: Diverse family photos or picture books
Simple drawings of family members
Optional: toy family figures

lessons.title: J'aime les animaux
lessons.oneGoal: Students will recognize common animal names and show preference with 'j'aime'

structure.opening: Quick family word review with gestures.
structure.mainActivity: Animal sounds and names - make animal sounds, students guess, then learn French names. Model 'J'aime les chats' with enthusiastic gestures.
structure.closing: Students choose their favorite animal and practice 'J'aime...' with support.

decisionPoints.then: Add colors - 'un chat noir', 'un chien rouge' (even if silly, they'll remember better).
Use sounds as memory aids - 'miaou' helps remember 'chat'.
Practice 'J'aime' vs 'Je n'aime pas' with exaggerated facial expressions.

whenThingsGoWrong.tooSillyWithSounds: Channel energy into the French words. 'That's right - CHAT!'
whenThingsGoWrong.cantChooseFavorite: That's fine! They can like all animals or just listen to others.
whenThingsGoWrong.pronunciationChallenges: Focus on meaning, not perfect pronunciation. Celebrate attempts.

materials: Animal pictures or toy animals
Animal sound audio or your own sound effects
Simple animal picture books

lessons.title: Dans ma classe
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify and point to classroom objects when named

structure.opening: Animal sounds review - quick and fun.
structure.mainActivity: Classroom scavenger hunt - name objects in French, students find and touch them. Start with obvious items.
structure.closing: Sit in circle, each student touches one classroom object while you say its French name.

decisionPoints.then: Add simple commands - 'Prenez un crayon' (take a crayon) with gestures.
Hold up actual objects while saying names. Point clearly to each item.
Have them bring you objects - 'Apportez-moi un livre' with gestures.

whenThingsGoWrong.cantFindObjects: Point directly to examples. Have backup objects ready on your desk.
whenThingsGoWrong.tooExcitedByHunt: Clear boundaries first. Practice walking vs running to objects.
whenThingsGoWrong.confusingSimilarWords: Use actions and pointing. Physical connection helps memory.

materials: Various classroom objects clearly visible
Backup set of key objects on your desk
Picture cards of objects if needed

lessons.title: Les parties du corps
lessons.oneGoal: Students will touch body parts when named and follow simple 'Touchez...' commands

structure.opening: Quick classroom objects review - point and name.
structure.mainActivity: Body parts song/game - 'Touchez votre tête' with actions. Start slow, build speed if they're ready.
structure.closing: Gentle stretching while naming body parts - helps them transition to next activity.

decisionPoints.then: Speed up the game or add combinations - 'Touchez votre tête et votre pied'.
Do actions very slowly and clearly. Use exaggerated movements.
Add simple dance moves or make it more like 'Heads and Shoulders'.

whenThingsGoWrong.studentsGetSilly: Keep them focused with your calm modeling. Make it respectful but fun.
whenThingsGoWrong.confusionWithCommands: Just do actions together without pressure. They'll follow along.
whenThingsGoWrong.someStudentsWithdraw: Invite participation but don't force. They can watch and learn.

materials: Open space for movement
Optional: simple body parts song or music
Your own body for clear modeling!

lessons.title: Qu'est-ce que c'est?
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand the question 'What is it?' and hear simple responses

structure.opening: Quick body parts warm-up - they love the movement.
structure.mainActivity: Mystery box or bag game - pull out familiar objects, ask 'Qu'est-ce que c'est?' Answer 'C'est un crayon' etc.
structure.closing: Students choose objects from around room, you ask question, class tries to answer together.

decisionPoints.then: Have them try asking the question to each other with your support.

decisionPoints.if: Students need more scaffolding with responses
decisionPoints.then: Show visual cards with 'C'est un...' and pictures. Point while speaking.
Add colors and numbers - 'C'est un crayon rouge', 'C'est deux livres'.

whenThingsGoWrong.questionTooLong: Break it down - just practice 'C'est un livre' for now.
whenThingsGoWrong.studentsGuessInEnglish: Great! Then repeat in French. They're understanding the concept.
whenThingsGoWrong.lostInterest: Make it sillier - put random objects in mystery bag, act surprised.

materials: Mystery box or opaque bag
Familiar classroom objects and toys
Visual cards with 'C'est un/une' if needed

lessons.title: Où est...?
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand location questions and respond through pointing/gestures

structure.opening: Quick 'Qu'est-ce que c'est?' review with a few objects.
structure.mainActivity: Hide and seek with objects - hide classroom items, ask 'Où est le crayon?' Students point and you say 'Ici!' or 'Là!'
structure.closing: Students hide objects for you to find. They get to ask 'Où est...?' with your support.

decisionPoints.then: Make hiding spots more creative. Add excitement with your reactions.
Add 'sur la table', 'sous la chaise' with clear gestures.

decisionPoints.if: Students want to ask the questions
decisionPoints.then: Support them heavily. Let them try with prompting.

whenThingsGoWrong.cantFindHiddenObjects: Hide them more obviously. Point if needed. Success is the goal.
whenThingsGoWrong.tooExcitedByHiding: Set clear rules about where things can be hidden. Keep it simple.
whenThingsGoWrong.confusedByLocationWords: Use very obvious gestures. Point clearly to 'ici' and 'là'.

materials: Small classroom objects that are easy to hide
Clear hiding spots that are safe and accessible
Your pointing finger and gestures!

lessons.title: Les émotions
lessons.oneGoal: Students will recognize emotion words and connect them to facial expressions

structure.opening: Quick location game - hide something obvious, let them find it.
structure.mainActivity: Emotion faces - show exaggerated facial expressions, name emotions in French. Use mirror if available for students to practice faces.
structure.closing: Emotion check-in - students show how they feel today with faces (no pressure to use French words yet).

decisionPoints.if: Students easily match emotions to expressions
decisionPoints.then: Add simple sentences - 'Je suis content' with appropriate faces.
Turn it into a game - make faces, others guess the emotion.
Support them in sharing - mix English and French as needed.

whenThingsGoWrong.studentsGetTooSilly: Acknowledge it's fun, then model serious faces respectfully.
whenThingsGoWrong.difficultTopicForSome: Keep it light and surface-level. No pressure to share personal feelings.
whenThingsGoWrong.vocabularyTooAbstract: Use very exaggerated expressions. Make it physical and obvious.

materials: Mirror for facial expressions
Emotion picture cards or drawings
Your own expressive face as the main tool

lessons.title: À l'école
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand school-related vocabulary and simple school rules

structure.opening: Quick emotion faces review - fun and connecting.
structure.mainActivity: School walk-through - point out parts of school, name them in French. Practice 'écouter' with listening games.
structure.closing: Simple school song or chant incorporating new vocabulary.

decisionPoints.if: Students connect school words to their experience
decisionPoints.then: Add simple school rules in French - 'Nous écoutons' while modeling listening.
Point to actual teacher, students, school building. Make it very visual.
Practice school greetings - how to say hello to other teachers in French.

whenThingsGoWrong.vocabularyTooAbstract: Use pictures and point to real examples. Teacher = you, élève = them.
whenThingsGoWrong.cantRememberNewWords: Repeat many times. Focus on one or two words only.
whenThingsGoWrong.restlessForSchoolTalk: Keep it brief. Add more movement and action.

materials: Pictures of school scenes
Actual school environment for pointing and naming
Simple song or chant about school

lessons.title: Mes vêtements
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify clothing items and understand 'Je porte...' statements

structure.opening: Quick school vocabulary review with pointing and actions.
structure.mainActivity: Clothing fashion show - students model their clothes while you name them in French. Introduce 'Je porte...' with gestures to self.
structure.closing: Clothing dance - call out clothing items, students touch those items on themselves.

decisionPoints.then: Let them try saying 'Je porte...' about their own clothes with support.
Add colors to clothing - 'Je porte un pantalon bleu'.

decisionPoints.if: Students connect easily to clothing words
decisionPoints.then: Describe other students' clothes - 'Marie porte une chemise rouge'.

whenThingsGoWrong.studentsFeelSelfConscious: Keep it positive and inclusive. Comment on everyone's clothes kindly.
whenThingsGoWrong.cantSeeClothingClearly: Use obvious examples - shoes, shirts. Point clearly.
whenThingsGoWrong.tooMuchNewVocabulary: Focus on just two clothing items. Quality over quantity.

materials: Students' own clothing as examples
Clothing picture cards as backup
Mirror for students to see themselves if available

lessons.title: La nourriture
lessons.oneGoal: Students will recognize food vocabulary and express simple preferences

structure.opening: Quick clothing review - point to your clothes and name them.
structure.mainActivity: Food pictures and preferences - show food pictures, name in French, students show thumbs up/down for 'j'aime' or 'je n'aime pas'.
structure.closing: Pretend picnic - lay out food pictures, students 'choose' foods for their imaginary lunch.

decisionPoints.then: Add 'j'aime manger...' as a complete phrase with eating gestures.
Add colors to foods - 'une pomme rouge', 'une pomme verte'.
Share simple French foods they might know - 'croissant', 'baguette'.

whenThingsGoWrong.culturalFoodDifferences: Honor all foods positively. Focus on the French words, not preferences.
whenThingsGoWrong.foodAllergiesOrSensitivities: Keep it to pictures only. No actual food needed.
whenThingsGoWrong.cantRememberFoodWords: Use obvious examples. Show picture while saying word multiple times.

materials: Clear pictures of common foods
Toy foods if available
Simple placemats or plates for pretend picnic

lessons.title: Les saisons
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify seasons and connect them to weather and activities

structure.opening: Quick food preferences review - show pictures, students react.
structure.mainActivity: Seasons pictures and actions - show season pictures, act out being hot/cold, name seasons in French.
structure.closing: Seasons movements - students act like they're in different seasons while you name them in French.

decisionPoints.then: Connect to clothing - 'En hiver, je porte...' showing warm clothes.
Add more weather actions - pretend snow, sun, swimming, etc.
Add activities - 'En été, je nage' with swimming motions.

whenThingsGoWrong.seasonsTooAbstract: Use obvious pictures and actions. Make temperature very physical.
whenThingsGoWrong.studentsFromDifferentClimates: Honor their experiences. Adapt examples to what they know.
whenThingsGoWrong.cantRememberSeasonWords: Focus on just hot/cold first. Add seasons gradually.

materials: Clear season pictures or drawings
Props for hot/cold actions (pretend to shiver, fan self)
Optional: different clothing items for seasons

lessons.title: Je peux...
lessons.oneGoal: Students will use 'je peux' to express what they can do with learned vocabulary

structure.opening: Quick seasons review with actions for hot and cold.
structure.mainActivity: Action demonstration - show actions like walking, running, then say 'Je peux marcher'. Students try actions and phrase with support.
structure.closing: Ability circle - each student demonstrates something they can do, you help them say 'Je peux...' in French.

decisionPoints.then: Connect to previous vocabulary - 'Je peux porter une chemise rouge'.
Add more actions - jumping, dancing, clapping with French words.
Let them combine learned words - 'Je peux toucher ma tête'.

whenThingsGoWrong.structureTooComplex: Just practice the actions with French words. Add 'je peux' later.
whenThingsGoWrong.studentsCantThinkOfAbilities: Suggest simple actions they've learned - pointing, walking, saying their name.
whenThingsGoWrong.sooMuchMovement: Channel energy into specific actions. Use calm voice to model.

materials: Open space for actions
List of actions you've learned in previous lessons
Encouraging attitude for all attempts

lessons.title: Mon histoire
lessons.oneGoal: Students will share simple personal information using learned vocabulary and structures

structure.opening: Quick 'Je peux...' review with actions they remember.
structure.mainActivity: Personal sharing circle - students share simple facts about themselves using learned French words with heavy support and modeling.
structure.closing: Class book creation - each student contributes one French sentence or word to a simple class book.

decisionPoints.if: Students confident to share in French
decisionPoints.then: Support longer sharing - name, favorite color, animal, etc.
Provide sentence starters and lots of prompting. Mix English and French.
Let them draw pictures and you describe in French what they show.

whenThingsGoWrong.studentsBlankOnVocabulary: Provide visual reminders of learned words. No pressure for perfection.
whenThingsGoWrong.tooShy: Sharing can be through actions, pointing, or drawings. Honor different comfort levels.
whenThingsGoWrong.wantToShareTooMuch: Gentle time limits. Celebrate what they share, then invite next person.

materials: Visual reminders of learned vocabulary
Paper and crayons for drawing if needed
Simple book or poster for class contributions

lessons.title: Nos amis
lessons.oneGoal: Students will describe classmates using learned vocabulary and practice social language

structure.opening: Quick personal sharing review - students remember something they shared yesterday.
structure.mainActivity: Friend descriptions - students work in pairs, describe each other using learned French words with your support and modeling.
structure.closing: Friendship circle - students say something kind about a classmate in simple French with help.

decisionPoints.then: Add more descriptive words they know - colors of clothing, things they like.
Model positive descriptions heavily. Focus on kind words only.
Support simple exchanges - 'Tu aimes...?' 'Oui, j'aime...' with prompting.

whenThingsGoWrong.socialConflictsArise: Keep focus on positive descriptions. Redirect any negativity immediately.
whenThingsGoWrong.studentsStuckOnDescriptions: Provide lots of prompts and examples. They can copy your models.
whenThingsGoWrong.shynessAboutCompliments: Model giving and receiving compliments. Keep it light and positive.

materials: Visual prompts for positive descriptive words
Mirror for students to practice expressions
Encouraging classroom environment

lessons.title: Notre classe française
lessons.oneGoal: Students will demonstrate their French learning through a simple class presentation or show

structure.opening: Quick friendship compliments review - spread positivity.
structure.mainActivity: French learning celebration - students demonstrate their favorite French words, songs, or phrases. Low pressure, high celebration.
structure.closing: Group celebration - everyone says 'Bravo!' and applauds their French learning journey together.

decisionPoints.then: Create mini-performance opportunities - songs, actions, or simple dialogues.
Do everything together as a group. No individual pressure.
Document their learning with photos or recordings (with permission).

whenThingsGoWrong.performanceAnxiety: Keep it completely optional. Celebrate observers as much as performers.
whenThingsGoWrong.forgetsLearning: Prompt with visual reminders. Focus on effort, not accuracy.
whenThingsGoWrong.tooMuchExcitement: Channel energy into organized celebration. Use calm transitions.

materials: Visual reminders of all learned vocabulary
Camera for documentation (optional)
Celebratory atmosphere and positive energy

lessons.title: Au revoir septembre
lessons.oneGoal: Students will reflect on their French learning journey and set intentions for continued learning

structure.opening: Final celebration review - quick showcase of favorite French learning.
structure.mainActivity: Learning reflection - students share (in English or French) their favorite French words or memories from the month.
structure.closing: Bridge to future - introduce 'octobre' and get excited about continuing French learning together.

decisionPoints.then: Preview some fun October vocabulary or activities to build anticipation.
Emphasize how much they've learned and how proud you are of their efforts.
Introduce idea of helping new French learners or teaching family members words.

whenThingsGoWrong.studentsReflectiontooAbstract: Ask specific questions - 'What was your favorite French animal?' etc.
whenThingsGoWrong.resistanceToFrench: Honor their feelings. Emphasize fun and choice in future learning.
whenThingsGoWrong.sadnessAboutEndingUnit: Reassure them French learning continues. This is just the beginning!

materials: All visual vocabulary from the month for review
Calendar showing September to October transition
Positive, encouraging attitude for the journey ahead

generalGuidance.timing: Lessons are flexible in length. Watch student attention and energy, not the clock.
generalGuidance.differentiation: Support ranges from just listening to full participation. Meet students where they are.
generalGuidance.assessment: Focus on engagement and effort over accuracy. Celebrate attempts and progress.
generalGuidance.materials: Most materials are common classroom items. Keep it simple and accessible.
generalGuidance.substituteTeacherNotes: Each lesson can stand alone. Read the decision points and adjust based on student response. When in doubt, do more modeling and less pressure for student output.
